title: fix(cli): the ownership ceremony names the uncomposed security plugin, never removal, for a shipped set or built-in position
body:
Fixes #23359
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`os migrate organization-ownership --apply` composes the security plugin only where `os serve` would: behind the auth gate, which needs `OS_AUTH_SECRET` or a development boot. That plugin declares the platform's shipped permission sets and the built-in positions. Run without a secret, the ceremony's catalog resolves none of them, and the ceremony blocked with a remedy that pointed at the rows, not at the cause.

Measured on `main` before this change: 4 remedy sentences in 2 steps, all from this one cause.

| step | rows | remedy printed before |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `rewrite` | a grant that names `admin_full_access` / `organization_admin_no_bypass` (the card's setup) | "Declare or author the set, or remove the grants, then re-run." |
| `rewrite` | a legacy grant (a 17.x database: `permission_set` empty) whose set row is `admin_full_access` | "The rewrite could not derive their name (see its notes); name or remove each, then re-run." |
| `authored-conversion` | the seeded `everyone` binding (the `repo:cloud#1` instance, `6167973978`) | "Declare the position (or remove the bindings), then re-run." |
| `rewrite` gate, under a wall | the same `everyone` binding | "The authored-conversion step carries them; resolve its blocker, then re-run." (that step only reports under a wall, so it has no blocker to resolve) |

The dispatch's mechanism hypothesis (a) named the first and third rows. I measured the second and fourth in the same function as the first (`verifyReferences`, the rewrite step's gate). Both have the same cause, and the second prints removal advice for a shipped set, which triage's ruling forbids ("Never print "remove the grants" for a shipped set."). So this PR covers all four. Each one is pinned, and each is listed under Acceptance notes.

## What changed

- **The composition fact comes from the boot and is never inferred.** `ApplyOptions.securityPlugin` carries `bootSchemaStack`'s own `composition.securityPlugin`, the same field `os migrate security-catalog-overlays` prints. The command passes it at the head of the `applyOrganizationOwnership` options literal (one line).
- **Names come from their owners.** `uncomposedSecurityRemedy` (in `organization-ownership-apply.ts`) answers only when the boot reported the plugin `composed: false` and the name is one the plugin declares:
  - shipped sets: `securityDefaultPermissionSets` (`@objectstack/plugin-security`), the list its manifest registers;
  - built-in positions: `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_NAMES` and `AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS` (`@objectstack/spec`), the two lists the plugin's `securityBuiltinPositions` is built from (that list is not exported).
- **One spelling.** The new remedy is `describeSecurityPluginComposition(status)`, followed by the one instruction that holds for every gate reason: "NAME is one of the permission sets it ships: keep the grants, and re-run where the security plugin is composed." For a position it says "built-in positions it declares" and "keep the bindings". No third spelling of the composition, and no edit to `schema-migration-plugins.ts`.
- **The legacy-grant case uses the rewrite's own decision.** `unnamedForComposition` reruns `planGrantRewrite` over the unnamed grants. Only its `unresolved` reason, for a shipped name, moves to the composition blocker ("their set row is NAME, which the security catalog does not resolve."). A grant unnamed for any other reason (no id, a missing row, another organization's row) keeps the general blocker.
- **Every step still refuses.** Nothing is resolved, skipped, guessed or deleted. A name the plugin does not declare keeps its remedy, and so does every name when the boot composed the plugin or did not say.

Measured once on a real boot with no secret (`bootSchemaStack` with the command's four composition flags, `NODE_ENV=production`, no `OS_AUTH_SECRET`; a throwaway file, deleted after the run and not committed): `composition.securityPlugin` was `{"composed":false,"reason":"no-secret"}`, and none of `admin_full_access`, `organization_admin_no_bypass` or `everyone` resolved. The card's two named grants then blocked with "1 grant(s) name the permission set admin_full_access, which the security catalog does not resolve (grant_admin). Did not compose the security plugin: `os serve` composes none here (no OS_AUTH_SECRET, and not a development boot: no --dev, and NODE_ENV is not development), so its shipped permission sets are not package-held names on this deployment's boot. admin_full_access is one of the permission sets it ships: keep the grants, and re-run where the security plugin is composed." `organization_admin_no_bypass` got the same sentence. A 17.x binding to `everyone` got the position form, in `authored-conversion` (single) and in the rewrite gate (isolated). A binding to the undeclared `zz_undeclared` kept today's remedy in both.

## Pins

- `organization-ownership-apply.test.ts`, describe "a name only the uncomposed security plugin declares". Each case reads its unknown-name control before its shipped name:
  - `rewrite`: grants naming `admin_full_access` and `organization_admin_no_bypass` get the composition and no "remove". A grant naming `zz_unknown_set` keeps "or remove the grants". Mirror deletion is not reached and nothing is deleted.
  - `rewrite`: a legacy grant whose set row is `admin_full_access` gets the composition and no "remove". A legacy grant on an unknown set row keeps "name or remove each".
  - `authored-conversion`: the `everyone` binding gets the composition and no "remove". `zz_undeclared` keeps "or remove the bindings".
  - the rewrite gate under a wall: the same binding pair.
  - controls (`composed: true`, and absent): both steps keep every remedy and print no composition sentence.
- `organization-ownership-apply.served-catalog.integration.test.ts`: the composed control on the real served boot. `composition.securityPlugin` is `{ composed: true }`, and the rewrite verifies grants naming `admin_full_access` and `organization_admin_no_bypass`, 2 of 2. Its `ceremony()` helper now passes the boot's own `securityPlugin`, as the command does.
- `organization-ownership.fate-supplement.integration.test.ts`: the command hands the boot's `composition.securityPlugin` to the apply step. The boot double gained the `composition` field the command now reads.

**Ablations** (`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, WRAP mode; restore proven as blob == HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`):

- **A.** Drop the composition branch (`if (!status || status.composed) return undefined;` becomes `return undefined;`). The 4 uncomposed pins go red at their shipped-name assertion (lines 2054, 2079, 2096, 2113), after their unknown-name assertions held. The 4 control cases stay green: `Tests 4 failed | 4 passed`. Restored to `d3dd0eda148f`.
- **B.** Drop the command's wiring line. The wiring pin goes red, and the file's other 8 stay green. Restored to `a4ce0f93c21f`.

## Verification

**On the final head `7d73667169`.** It merges `origin/main` `fba37122b0`, which touches only `packages/lint`; that package was rebuilt.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0, including `check:test-typecheck`.
- Integration project, the three touched suites (apply, served-catalog, fate-supplement): `Tests 101 passed`.
- ESLint on the five changed TypeScript files, with `pnpm lint`'s own `--no-inline-config`: exit 0. This is a narrowed `pnpm lint`; why that is sound is under Acceptance notes.
- Gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 65 commands.
  - 63 exited 0.
  - `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET), because this worktree has no full `pnpm build`. NOT MEASURED locally: CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs both.
  - `--ran` with each exit code recorded: "65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 63 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)", 0 UNRUN.

**On `563552a332`.** The source is the same; the later commits only reorder assertions in one test file and add the changeset and the merge.

- `@objectstack/cli` unit project, the whole of it: `286 passed` files, `4286 passed | 29 skipped` tests. Two suites first failed for a missing prerequisite ("packages/cli is not built"), so they were not measured on that run. After `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build` they passed (36 tests, with `organization-ownership.apply-flags.test.ts`).
- Integration project, every file that reaches the changed modules (apply, served-catalog, not-declared, one-shot-family, fate-supplement, column-drops): `Test Files 6 passed`, `Tests 195 passed`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Scope beyond the two named sites.** The two added sentences are in the `rewrite` step's own gate (`verifyReferences`), where no other claim holds code. Without them, a 17.x database (legacy grants) or a walled posture would keep the card's defect.
- **The control route.** The composed control runs on `OS_AUTH_SECRET` (the served-catalog suite's existing boot), not on `NODE_ENV=development`. The auth gate answers `{ composed: true }` on either route, and no second boot was added.
- **No committed no-secret real-boot pin.** The served-catalog suite measured `Duration 28.28s`, of which `import 23.29s`, so a second file would pay that load again. The chain is pinned in three links: the boot's no-secret answer (`security-catalog-overlays.integration.test.ts`, existing), the command's wiring (new), and the remedy given the answer (new). The real no-secret boot was measured once (above).
- **`describeSecurityPluginComposition`'s no-secret reason names `--dev`.** `--dev` is `os serve`'s flag; this command has none. It is left unchanged, as the dispatch requires: `schema-migration-plugins.ts` is reused, not edited.
- **The rewrite's notes are unchanged.** The note "unnamed grant(s) point at a set row whose name the security catalog does not resolve" still lists a shipped-set grant without the cause. The blocker beside it now names the cause.
- **Why narrowing `pnpm lint` to the changed files is sound.** Three facts:
  1. the changed TypeScript files are exactly those five (`dispatch-gates` change set, merge base `fba37122b`);
  2. `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware or cross-file rule ("never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file"), so no other file's verdict can move;
  3. the run used `pnpm lint`'s own `--no-inline-config` and exited 0.

  CI runs the full `pnpm lint`.
- **Out of scope, found while measuring, reported to the seat and not changed here.** Under a wall, a 17.x binding to a position no catalog declares blocks the rewrite gate with "The authored-conversion step carries them; resolve its blocker". With the plugin composed or not, that step only reports under a wall, so it has no blocker to resolve. The `zz_undeclared` cases above reproduce it.
